newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firmer after quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firmer after quiet trade.

text.p: The Mexican peso ended slightly firmer on Monday after recovering from short-lived dollar buying and following what traders said was a calm session due to lack of fresh economic data.
"We have no data and you cannot trade when that happens," a dealer said. "We are all waiting for the second half of June before buying (dollars); even so I don't see the dollar weakening much."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 0.55 and 0.6 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.9150/7.9165 and 7.9105/7.9130 per dollar.
Dealers said the peso had softened in early trade due to speculative dollar buying, which faded at mid-session when dealers saw the peso failed to weaken further.
Trading volume could pick up during the second half of June, dealers added, due to the close of the first half and approaching mid-terms on July 6.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed one centavo firmer at 7.9130/7.9160 per dollar.
The peso also closed firmer on market forecasts bellwether 28-day Cetes rates could gain by up to 25 basis points at the central bank's primary auction of government securities on Tuesday.
"Primary rates could increase a little, which should help the peso to trade at between 7.9050/7.9300 per dollar all week," another trader said.
